guide.summary: Public OAuth app, customers' admins enable it (approval path unconfirmed); Free developer account, own testing (self-serve, wait none); Listing in Box Integrations Center and partner program (approval path unconfirmed). Where the path is unconfirmed, the agent did not find it in the provider's docs.
guide.verdict: Free developer account, own testing (self-serve, wait none).

composio.note: Composio manages OAuth2 for Box, so prototypes need no own app. A separate Box MCP toolkit requires your own OAuth app.

need_own_app.answer: Not for a prototype, since Composio provides a managed Box app. For launch you need your own app if you want your brand on the consent screen, your own scopes, or a dedicated quota.
reasons: Managed app consent screen says Composio wants to access the account, not your brand
Managed apps share quota across all Composio users; your own app gets a dedicated quota
Default managed scopes may not cover everything you need
Custom auth config allows branding, scopes, rate limits and polling intervals

prerequisites.title: Free Box developer account
prerequisites.detail: It gives access to the Developer Console, where OAuth 2.0 apps are created.

prerequisites.title: Client ID for the customer's admin
prerequisites.detail: A Box Admin or Co-Admin needs your app's Client ID to authorize it in the Admin Console.

steps.title: Create a User-type app
steps.detail: Log into the Developer Console, select New App, choose User as app type, then Create.
steps.done_when: The app exists with a client ID and secret.

steps.title: Copy redirect URI from Composio
steps.detail: Copy the redirect URI from the Composio dashboard and add it under OAuth 2.0 Redirect URI in the Configuration tab. It must be HTTPS and match exactly.
steps.done_when: Redirect URI is saved in Box.

steps.title: Select scopes
steps.detail: Draft the minimum scopes your agent needs and set them at app creation. Scopes work together with user permissions.
steps.done_when: Scopes are saved in the Configuration tab.

steps.title: Create Composio auth config
steps.detail: Create the Box auth config through Composio's API using your own client ID and secret.

steps.title: Submit app for admin approval
steps.detail: Enterprise developers submit from the Configuration or Enablement tab. The Primary Admin gets an email to approve.

steps.title: Wait for Box Admin approval
steps.detail: The admin adds the app by Client ID in the Admin Console Platform Apps tab. No wait time is documented.
steps.done_when: The app is enabled for the enterprise.

traps.title: A new enterprise can authorize up to 10,000 custom
traps.detail: A new enterprise can authorize up to 10,000 custom apps.

traps.title: Changing scopes needs re-authorization
traps.detail: Admin authorization is a snapshot, so scope changes take effect only after a Box Admin re-authorizes. Free developer accounts re-authorize automatically on save.

traps.title: Redirect URI must match exactly
traps.detail: With several redirect URIs, omitting redirect_uri gives a redirect_uri_missing error. Duplicate URIs cannot be saved.

traps.title: Refresh tokens expire
traps.detail: Access tokens last 60 minutes and refresh tokens 60 days or one use. Plan token refresh in the agent.

traps.title: Composio callback domain cannot be verified by you
traps.detail: Box's docs do not show redirect-domain verification, so this is likely unneeded. To hide Composio's domain, proxy the callback through your own domain with a 302 redirect.

traps.title: OAuth app cannot become a server app
traps.detail: If you need server authentication later, create a new app and pick Server.

blockers.symptom: Customer cannot use the app: admin has not enabled it
blockers.what_it_means: The customer's Box Admin decides whether unpublished apps are enabled by default and may need to enable yours.
blockers.what_to_do: Give the admin your Client ID and the Admin Console steps: Platform tab, Platform Apps, Add.
blockers.agent_can_help: Draft the instructions email for the customer admin.
